correctness.rationale: The zero-sum incidence eigenvector of the triangular graph yields a negative-type lower bound for every ℓ1 embedding after S_n symmetrization. Exact combinatorial orbit counts for Hamiltonian-cycle cuts produce a finite-dimensional ℓ1 metric at precisely the lower bound for all n>=6; no finite experiment is promoted to an infinite proof. 8,462 supplementary exact integer/rational checks independently confirm graph distances, incidence algebra, crossing counts and small complete permutation orbits.

value.rationale: The graph shortest-path ℓ1 distortion is a meaningful structural invariant. For every n>=6 the exact rational optimum strictly increases from 4/3 to 2, is attained by a canonical orbit of Hamiltonian-cycle cuts, and saturates a nontrivial incidence-eigenspace obstruction. The result solves a natural infinite family, is not an isolated census entry, and creates a reusable connection between metric cut-cone witnesses and spectral negative type. No broad downstream theorem is claimed.
